html:
On 13 May 1969, days after an election in which opposition parties gained, riots between Malays and Chinese broke out in Kuala Lumpur. The official toll was 196 dead; other accounts put it higher.

Parliament was suspended and a National Operations Council ruled for almost two years. Tunku Abdul Rahman stepped down, and Abdul Razak took over.

The government blamed the gap in wealth between Malays and the Chinese. It answered with the New Economic Policy, with quotas favouring Malays and other Bumiputera, and widened the ruling coalition. The memory of 13 May still hangs over talk of race in Malaysia. See Chinese migration.
sum: On 13 May 1969, days after an election in which opposition parties gained, riots between Malays and Chinese broke out in Kuala Lumpur. The official toll was 196 dead; other accounts put it higher.
